changes: Zoom-out, orbit rotation and upward parallax use one smoothed scroll progress and one eased phase in both WebGL and WebGPU.
Framing fits the base zoom before applying the shared zoom-out factor, preventing the early zoom plateau that delayed zoom relative to rotation.
The map and hero share a width-based stage with an 840px desktop minimum and a 930px mobile minimum, independent of window height.
Phones show the complete centered sea plate; desktop retains its permanent slight right-tip crop from the initial pose.
One 85% content veil keeps the map visible as background decoration after the intro.
preserved: all existing lighting and reflection effects
checks: Production build and full npm test suite pass.
Camera tests verify zoom and orbit share the same phase.
Prepared-world framing tests verify actual zoom decreases from the first scroll sample across eight desktop and mobile stage sizes, without vertical clipping or pose drift.
Browser QA: complete mobile framing at 390x844; desktop map stage unchanged between 1280x600 and 1280x1000; initial, intermediate and work poses checked at 1919x1286.
Browser confirms the canvas has no CSS translation and the content veil alpha is 0.85; temporary viewport overrides were reset.
